subject: research/grasp-twin
professional: a robotic grasping researcher reviewing for ICRA / IEEE RA-L (grasp force optimisation and robust grasping under contact uncertainty). They would check first: is the slip/crush model physically right for a two-finger pinch (friction cone, per-finger load), is the closed-form optimum actually the global optimum, does the Monte Carlo agree, are the plug-in/delta-method numbers converged, what is the nearest prior work (grasp force optimisation, robust grasp quality under friction uncertainty, value-of-the-stochastic-solution / estimate-then-optimise), and is anything here new or tested on real grasp data

evidence.correctness: Recomputed with scipy 1.18 / numpy, importing nothing from grasp_twin (scratchpad indep.py). Base optimum: scipy bounded minimiser + brentq on my hand-derived J'(x) = -phi(u)/s + phi(v)/r gives x* 1.3976935, F* 4.0459 w0, J* 0.013731 (slip 0.00942, crush 0.00431) = results.txt; numpy.roots of the hand-derived stationarity quadratic (x+m)^2/s^2-(x-f)^2/r^2 = 2 ln(r/s) gives 1.39769349 (and 2.918, a maximum). Too-clean twin rows (s_twin 0.2/0.1/0.05: F 3.718/3.121/2.652, twin J 1.68e-3/1.09e-5/3.45e-8, real J 0.02010/0.06901/0.17354, 0.5/4.0/11.6 x J*), bias rows (delta -0.3/+0.15/+0.3: regret 0.01168/0.00208/0.00778), and DR width (continuous optimum 0.4668 for +0.3, regret 0.02017 at -0.3 for w=0.47) all match. Delta method with analytic implicit-function derivatives (J''=2.1379, dx/dm=-0.3089, dx/ds=0.5939; Fisher variances s^2/n, s^2/2n) gives 0.00523 (n=5), 0.00052 (50), 0.00003 (1000) = results.txt. numpy Monte Carlo at x*+0.3, 1e7 grasps: slip 0.000414, crush 0.26544 vs exact 0.00041 / 0.26529. Not 4: the small-n plug-in means are single 2000-fit draws of a heavy-tailed regret; 40,000 fits with the author's own code give 0.01216 +/- 0.00013 at n=5 (reported 0.01094 +/- 0.00052, 2.3 se low), and my numpy redraw 0.01227 +/- 0.00047, so delta/mean at n=5 is 0.43 not 0.48, and 0.93 (not 0.95) at n=50.

Everything claimed as done runs end to end. Stale: README:10 says run.py takes ~1 min, it takes 2.0 s.
evidence.verification: Tests pass (7 OK in 0.4 s). They check the closed form against the author's own numeric search, FOC, Monte Carlo agreement, regret signs and orderings, the local-quadratic ratio, width compensation, and the delta method at n=400 only. Five mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 3 caught (Var s_hat s^2/2n -> s^2/n; sign of the log-weight term in the quadratic; min -> max over candidate roots), 2 survived: fit_plugin's variance divisor n -> n-1 (model.py:102, changes every small-n calibration number) and run.py:26 plateau upper edge 3 sd -> 2 sd (changes the headline 'real slip 0.015' number). No test pins results.txt, run.py is untested, and nothing tests small-n plug-in regret or the plateau numbers that the README headlines.
evidence.craft: Read src/grasp_twin/model.py (123 lines), tests/test_model.py, experiments/run.py, figure.py, pyproject.toml. Stdlib only, small pure functions, figure parsed from results.txt rather than retyped, honest docstrings about the plateau. Defects: x_star filters roots by a finite-difference second derivative with e=1e-5 (model.py:58-59) that returns exactly 0.0 when the loss is ~1e-11 at the true minimum, so x_star returns None (seen on a real n=5 plug-in fit, s_hat=0.033, and on 248 of 3000 random parameter sets); the grid fallback hides it. x_star also returns an interior local minimum that is worse than the boundary 'do not grip / accept crush' limits (10 of 3000 random parameter sets, e.g. Ls 0.97, Lc 3.58), contradicting its docstring. run.py recomputes J'' by hand instead of reusing the module; `from grasp_twin.model import *` in tests and run.py; empty __init__.py.
evidence.claims: Checked against results.txt and recomputation: the headline numbers (F* 4.05, J* 0.0137, 1.1e-5 vs 0.069, 4.0x, 11.6x, 2/15/57/85% bias costs, width 0.47, 0.020 = 1.5x J*, the plug-in means) are all in results.txt and recompute. Wrong or unbacked: (1) README:3 says the delta method 'over-predicts at small n, e.g. 0.48x at n=5'; delta/mean = 0.48 means it under-predicts, as the white paper (whitepaper.md:17) correctly says. (2) README:3 and whitepaper.md:17 'within 5% for n >= 50' rests on one 2000-fit draw; at 40,000 fits the ratio is 0.932 at n=50 and 0.961 at n=100, so the threshold is n >= 100. (3) README:10 '~1 min' for run.py, actual 2.0 s. (4) model.py:42 docstring 'cannot happen for positive weights with -m < f' is false (None on 8% of random positive-weight parameter sets with -m < f, including a base-case plug-in fit). (5) README:3 'upper edge ... real slip 0.015' is a point the author chose (3 crush-sd below the median crush force, run.py:26), not an edge of the twin's plateau; the white paper says so, the README and live page do not. Limits paragraph and 'chosen, not measured' caveat are present and candid; no affiliation claimed with the HIRO group.
evidence.fitness: Job: a grasping or sim-to-real researcher wanting to build on 'what a too-clean friction twin does to grip force'. What is here is a one-dimensional newsvendor-style decision (two log-normal CDF risks in ln F) solved in closed form and probed at one chosen parameter point with no grasp data. Nearest prior work, none cited: grasp force optimisation (Kerr & Roth 1986, IJRR; Buss, Hashimoto & Moore 1996, IEEE T-RA), robust grasp quality under friction uncertainty (Zheng & Qian 2005, IEEE T-RO; Mahler et al. 2017 Dex-Net 2.0, RSS, which samples friction to compute robust grasp success probability), human grip-force safety margins (Johansson & Westling 1984), and the operations-research results the findings restate: a deterministic or under-dispersed model's regret is the value of the stochastic solution (Birge 1982), and plug-in regret ~ 1/2 J'' Var(x_hat) is the standard estimate-then-optimise / operational-statistics analysis (Liyanage & Shanthikumar 2005; Elmachtoub & Grigas 2022). The derivation is sound, but the result is not new beyond a worked example, it is one of ~130 near-identical *-twin projects that research/PROGRAMMES.md:8-13 itself says 'few would stand alone as a thesis chapter', and it is not part of a programme (sim2real-inference subsumes the question). A reviewer would reject it in the first read for novelty and absence of real contact data.
evidence.domain: Against Murray, Li & Sastry (1994) ch. 5 and standard grasp-force practice: the per-finger slip condition mu F >= W(1+a)/2 is the right Coulomb condition for a symmetric two-finger pinch with the load tangential (pass). Departures a grasping reviewer would hit: one friction coefficient shared by both contacts (independent per-contact friction makes slip the weaker of two, changing the slip law); no torsional/soft-finger friction or off-centre centre of mass (rotational slip is the common failure for glassware); crush modelled as a normal-force threshold rather than contact stress/area; force set open-loop with no slip sensing, while real fragile-object grasping uses tactile reflexes (acknowledged in Limitations); log-normal friction spread 0.3 and crush at 6 w0 with r=0.15 are invented, with no measurement or citation; regret asymmetry and width-compensation conclusions are drawn from one parameter point (acknowledged). Method correct for the toy; not a method a practitioner would use to set grip force.

verdict: A tidy, reproducible closed-form toy whose arithmetic is right and whose research contribution is thin. Every headline number recomputes independently with scipy/numpy (x* 1.3976935, J* 0.013731, the too-clean-twin rows 4.0x and 11.6x J*, bias regrets, width 0.47 and its 0.020 regret at the opposite bias, the delta-method values via analytic implicit derivatives, and 1e7-grasp Monte Carlo), and run.py and figure.py reproduce their committed outputs byte for byte; the live page serves them. It misses the bar on claims, verification and fitness: the README says the delta method over-predicts at small n when it under-predicts, 'within 5% for n >= 50' fails at n=50 once the heavy-tailed plug-in regret is averaged over 40,000 fits (0.93), 2 of 5 seeded mutants survive because nothing pins results.txt, and x_star's finite-difference curvature test returns None at real minima despite its docstring. A grasping reviewer would find the slip condition correct but the model (shared friction, no torsional slip, invented spreads, no data) a worked example, and the findings a restatement of grasp-force-optimisation and value-of-the-stochastic-solution results it does not cite.
